title: quarter-end-ignite-playbook-exec-talking-points-v0-1
content:
Purpose and audience: quick working playbook to align exec and comms leads for the quarter-end all-hands and the Q1 OKR primer. This is a tactical doc — living, iterative. Use for rehearsal, speaker timing, and last-mile alignment.

Top-level goals for the deck and town: (what the CEO wants to land)
- Reinforce the mission: move from early growth to predictable inference platform for production customers.
- Signal where we will invest next quarter: reliability (SLA), Dedicated capacity scale, Private deployments pilots.
- Surface one measurable customer outcome per product vertical (hosted API, dedicated, private).
- End with clear asks: two priorities for every team and where exec support is needed.

OKR draft (company-level) — working numbers, will refine with product/finance: (Goal statements + candidate KRs)
1) Goal: Deliver predictable, enterprise-grade inference that reduces customer latency variance by 50%
   - KR1: Median 95th percentile token latency across top-10 hosted models reduced by 40% relative to baseline quarter start
   - KR2: Achieve <1% error rate for model routing fallbacks in production for top 25 customers
   - KR3: Launch Dedicated capacity SLA beta for 3 anchor customers with contractual latency SLOs

2) Goal: Improve unit economics for production workloads by 30% via batching, quantization, and caching
   - KR1: Reduce average cost-per-1k-tokens for high-throughput workloads by 25% on dedicated pools
   - KR2: Ship model quantization profiles for 5 commonly-used model families and measure perf/cost delta
   - KR3: Deploy caching prefix policy to cover 20% of tokens for top-20 customers by request pattern

3) Goal: Make Private deployments frictionless for regulated customers
   - KR1: Complete VPC onboarding automation with step-by-step docs and one-click key rotation for 5 major cloud partners
   - KR2: Deliver on-prem packaging and internal QA automation for air-gapped installs (pilot w/2 customers)
   - KR3: Publish SOC2+ readiness checklist and close top 10 compliance gaps identified by audits

Notes on framing these OKRs in the all-hands: keep language concrete and customer-outcome oriented. Avoid low-level engineering metric dumping — use 1–2 vivid examples of customer impact each.

Exec update bullets (for the CEO + CTO segments)
- CEO (6 minutes): macro signal on market, strategy posture: "We win by serving — not by model ownership. Our priority is predictable, economical inference at scale." Call out: 1 headline metric (net revenue retention or number of customers in Dedicated) and 1 customer story.
- CTO (8 minutes): critical infra wins and roadmap: highlight serving-runtime optimizations shipped this quarter (continuous batching, KV cache improvements), what shipped and what remains. Callouts: any incidents and mitigations (concise), Dedicated capacity progress, and Private deployment milestones.
- Head of Product (6 minutes): product launches and the operational playbook (rollouts, rollbacks, tracing hooks). Quick demo of Console dashboard change (15–20s screen grab).

All-hands run-of-show (45 minutes total)
- 0:00–0:05 Opening: CEO quick welcome and 1-line mission anchor
- 0:05–0:13 CTO update: infra wins + what’s blocked (8 min + 2 Qs)
- 0:13–0:19 Product update: roadmap highlights + demo (6 min)
- 0:19–0:28 Customer spotlight (pre-recorded 6 min + 3 live Qs)
- 0:28–0:36 People & org updates (hiring, updates to on-call, SRE rotations) (8 min)
- 0:36–0:42 OKR primer and priority asks (6 min)
- 0:42–0:45 Closing + immediate community asks (3 min)

Rehearsal checklist (to be completed at least 48h before)
- Confirm slides final and deck exported with correct aspect ratio (owner: Design)
- AV check for CEO/CTO/pre-record (owner: Events)
- Speaker notes loaded into shared slide comments (owner: Exec EA)
- Prepare 3 starter Qs for live Q&A, route to comms lead (owner: Comms)
- Slack reminder + calendar invite with run-of-show (owner: Ops)

Talking points for CEO (condensed)
- Opening: "This quarter we focused on solidifying the platform foundations so our customers can rely on us for production inference."
- Market posture: "As models proliferate, winners are those who deliver predictable cost, latency, and reliability."
- Wins to call out: Dedicated capacity pilot, two Private pilots onboarding, measurable latency improvements for key customers.
- Ask to org: Each team picks one unit-economics improvement and one reliability improvement to own next quarter.

Talking points for CTO (condensed)
- What shipped: continuous batching improvements (x tokens/sec), KV cache latency reduction (y ms), new kernel selection heuristics rolled to 3 regions.
- Incidents and mitigation: short incident timeline + permanent mitigations; no finger-pointing, emphasize learning and follow-up.
- Near-term blockers: hardware variance in partner regions, work to widen quantization testing matrix.

Risk register (brief):
- Risk: Burst capacity shortages during holiday traffic
  Mitigation: pre-scheduled Dedicated buffer; cross-region failover playbook (owner: infra ops)
- Risk: Regressions after quantization changes impacting output quality
  Mitigation: expand evaluation harnesses, QA gate before rollout (owner: applied-ml)
- Risk: Private deploy onboarding delays due to partner network configurations
  Mitigation: create one-page runbook per major cloud (owner: private-deployments team)

Open questions for exec sync (items to resolve pre-deck freeze)
- Finalize company-level KR targets: finance to confirm cost baseline numbers by 2025-11-25 (owner: Finance liaisons)
- Agree on the single CEO headline metric for the town (NRR vs Dedicated anchor customers)
- Decide whether to include a product roadmap swimlane for "research model onboarding" or keep it internal to applied-ml

Action table (quick)
- Finalize slides + QA export: Design, due 2025-11-25
- Finance baseline confirm: Lina (Finance), due 2025-11-24
- AV rehearsal: Events, due 2025-12-01
- CEO/CTO dry run: Exec EA, due 2025-12-01
- Publish final talk track + slack thread (Comms), due 2025-12-02

Appendix (notes to self / comms drafts)
- Short comms draft for product blog: 2–3 paragraphs emphasizing reliability and cost wins; link to customer case studies.
- FAQ starters for town Q&A: pricing questions, Dedicated SLA eligibility, Private deployment timelines, bug/regression policies.

Tone guidance: be candid, engineering-forward, and outcome-oriented. Use customer stories to humanize technical wins. If an ask involves reprioritization, state the tradeoff explicitly (e.g., "We will pause feature X to accelerate SLA work for Dedicated pilots").

Versioning: this is v0-1 internal playbook. Drop comments inline in this doc; major changes should be captured in tracked Confluence page referenced above.

Unresolved (capture for next sync)
- Which two Dedicated anchor customers do we name in the deck? Ops to confirm list by EOD 2025-11-20.
- QA signal for quantized models: what metric threshold triggers rollback? Applied-ML + QA to propose by 2025-11-27.

If you're editing: append initials and date beside any substantive change.

End of draft.
